{{Short description|Statistician}}
'''Eva Eisenberg Jacobs''' (January 17, 1921 &ndash; April 28, 2015){{r|wapo}} was a statistician with the U.S. [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]] who edited their ''Handbook of U. S. Labor Statistics''{{r|core}} and headed their Division of Consumer Expenditure Surveys.{{r|wapo|oppenheim}}

Eva Eisenberg was born in [[New York City]], and joined the government service in 1942, studying productivity and economic growth at the [[United States Department of Labor|Labor Department]]. 
She became chief of Consumer Expenditure Surveys beginning in 1972, and retired in 1993. In her retirement, she edited the ''Handbook of U.S. Labor Statistics'' from 1997 to 2008.{{r|wapo}}

In 1982, Jacobs was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fasa}} In 1998, the Business and Economic Statistics Section of the [[American Statistical Association]] gave her their Julius Shiskin Award{{r|wapo|shiskin}} "for her management of the Consumer Expenditure Survey Program, her work on the use of the [[Consumer Expenditure Survey]] data to analyze and interpret the economy, and her responsiveness to customer needs".{{r|shiskin}}

She died at age 94, of complications of congestive heart failure, in [[Bethesda, Maryland]], on April 28, 2015.{{r|wapo}}
